source_text: Ad prandium uel ad cenam quales uocari iubet? quales ostenderat per Esaiam: confringe panem tuum esurienti. et mendicos et qui sine tecto sunt induc in domum tuam, qui scilicet humanitatis istius uicem retribuere non possint. hanc si Christus captari uetat, in resurrectione eam repromittens, creatoris est forma, cui non placent amantes munera, sectantes retributionem. Etiam inuitatoris parabola cui magis parti occurrat, expende. homo quidam fecit cenam et uocauit multos. utique cenae paratura uitae aeterna saturitatem figurat. dico primo extraneos et nullius iuris adfines inuitari ad cenam non solere, certe facilius solere domesticos et familiares. ergo creatoris est inuitasse, ad quem pertinebant qui inuitabantur, et per Adam, qua homines, et (per) patres, qua Iudaici, non eius, ad quem neque natura pertinebant neque praerogatiua. dehinc si is mittit ad conuiuas, qui cenam parauit, sic quoque creatoris est cena, qui misit ad conuiuas admonendos, ante iam uocatos per patres, admonendos autem per prophetas, non, qui neminem miserit ad monendum nec qui nihil prius egerit ad uocandum, sed ipse descenderit subito, tantum quod innotescens iam inuitans, tantum quod inuitans iam in conuiuium cogens, eandem faciens horam cenandi et ad cenam inuitandi. excusant se inuitati. si ab alio deo, merito, quia subito inuitati; si non merito, ergo nec subito; si autem non subito inuitati, ergo a creatore, a quo olim, cuius denique declinauerant uocationem tunc, primo dicentes ad Aaronem: fac nobis deos, qui praeeant nobis, atque exinde aure audientes et non audientes, uocationem scilicet dei, qui pertinentissime ad hanc parabolam per Hieremiam: audite, inquit, uocem meam, et ero uobis in deum et uos mihi in populum, et ibitis in omnibus uiis meis, quascumque mandauero uobis — ecce inuitatio dei — et non audierunt, inquit, et non aduerterunt aurem suam m, - ecce recuaatio populi - 8 e sed i e abieruntin his, quae concupiuerunt corde suo malo: \'agrum emi\' et \'boues mercatus sum\' et \'uxorem duxi ? . et adhuc ingerit: et emisi omnes ad uos famulos meos, prophetas, — hic erit spiritus sanctus, admonitor conuiuarum — die et ante lucem, et non audiit populus meus et non intendit auribus suis et obdurauit collum suum. hoc ut patri familiae renuntiatum est, motus tunc — bene quod et motus; negat enim Marcion moueri deum suum; ita et hoc meus est — mandat de plateis et uicis ciuitatis facere sublectionem. uideamus an eo sensu, quo rursus per Hieremiam: numquid solitudo factus sum domui Israhelis aut terra in incultum derelicta? — id est: numquid non habeo quos adlegam aut unde adlegam? — quoniam dixit populus meus: non uenimus ad te. itaque misit ad alios uocandos ex eadem adhuc ciuitate. dehinc loco abundante praecepit etiam de uiis et sepibus colligi, id est nos iam de extraneis gentibus, illa scilicet aemulatione, qua in Deuteronomio: auertam meam faciemab eis et monstrabo, quid illis in nouissimis, — id est alios possessuros locum eorum — . quoniam genitura peruersa est, filii in quibus fides non est. illi obaemulati sunt me in non deo et prouocauerunt me in iram in idolis suis, e t ego obaemulabor eos in non natione, (in natione) insipienti prouocabo eos in iram, in nobis scilicet, quorum spem Iudaei gemunt, de qua illos gustaturos negat dominus, derelicta Sione tamquam specula in uinea et in cucumerario casula, posteaquam et nouissimam in Christo inuitationem recusauit. quid ex hoc ordine, secundum dispositiones et praedicationes creatoris recensendo, competere potest illi, cuius nec ordo habet nec dispositio ad parabolae conspirationem, qui totum opus semel fecit? aut quae erit prima uocatio eius, et quae secundo actu admonitio? ante debent alii excusare, postea alii conuenisse. nunc autem pariter utramque partem inuitare uenit, de ciuitate, de sepibus, aduersus speculum parabolae. nec potest iam fastidiosos iudicare quos numquam retro inuitauit, quos cum maxime adgreditur. aut si de futuro eos iudicat contempturos uocationem, ergo et sublectionem loco eorum ex gentibus de futuro portendit. plane adhuc secundo uenturus est: [ut gentibus praedicet. et si] uenturus est autem, puto, non quasi uocaturus adhuc conuiuas, sed iam collocaturus. interea qui cenae istius uocationem in caeleste conuiuium interpretaris spiritalis saturitatis et iocunditatis, memento et terrenas promissiones uini et olei et frumenti et ipsius ciuitatis aeque in spiritalia figurari a creatore.
pass_a_gloss: To lunch or to dinner, what kind of people does He command to be called? What kind of people did He show through Isaiah: Break your bread for the hungry. And bring in the poor and those who are without a roof into your house, who, of course, cannot repay the kindness of this humanity. If Christ forbids being captured, promising it in the resurrection, it is the Creator's form, to whom those who love gifts are not pleasing, but rather those who follow retribution. Also, in the parable of the inviter, to whom it may occur more, let us spend. A certain man made a dinner and called many. Certainly, the preparation of the dinner of eternal life figures saturation. I say first that strangers and those who are of no right are not usually called to dinner, but rather domestics and family members are usually called. Therefore, it is the Creator's to have invited, to whom those who were invited belonged, and through Adam, inasmuch as they are men, and through the fathers, inasmuch as they are Jews, not to the one to whom neither nature nor prerogative belonged. Then, if He sends to the guests who were invited, who prepared the dinner, thus also the dinner is the Creator's, who sent to the guests to be admonished, who were already called through the fathers, to be admonished, however, through the prophets, not the one who sent no one to admonish nor who did nothing prior to call, but rather He Himself descended suddenly, only in that He was already inviting, only in that He was inviting, already forcing into the banquet, making the same hour for dining and for being invited to dinner. The invited ones excuse themselves. If from another god, deservedly, because they were invited suddenly; if not deservedly, therefore not suddenly; but if not suddenly invited, therefore from the Creator, from whom long ago, whose call they had declined then, first saying to Aaron: Make gods for us, who may precede us, and from then on, hearing with the ear and not hearing, the call of God, who pertains most closely to this parable through Jeremiah: Hear, He says, my voice, and I will be a god to you and you to me a people, and you will go in all my ways, which I command you — behold, the invitation of God — and they did not hear, He says, and they did not turn their ear — behold, the refusal of the people — but they went away in the things which they desired in their evil heart: 'I bought a field' and 'I bought oxen' and 'I took a wife.' And still He presses: And I sent all my servants, the prophets, to you — here will be the Holy Spirit, the admonisher of the guests — saying and before the light, and my people did not hear and did not attend with their ears and hardened their neck. This was announced to the head of the family, then moved — well that He was also moved; for He denies that His god is moved; thus this is mine — He commands to make a collection from the streets and alleys of the city. Let us see if in that sense, again through Jeremiah: Has the house of Israel become a wilderness to me or a land abandoned to desolation? — that is: Do I not have those to call or from where to call? — because my people said: We will not come to you. Therefore, He sent to call others from the same city still. Then, in a place abundant, He also commanded to collect from the roads and hedges, that is, we now from the foreign nations, that emulation, of course, with which in Deuteronomy: I will turn my face away from them and show them what will be in the last times — that is, others will possess their place — because the generation is perverse, sons in whom there is no faith. They emulated me in a non-god and provoked me to anger in their idols, and I will emulate them in a non-nation, (in a nation) foolish, I will provoke them to anger, in us, of course, whose hope the Jews lament, from which the Lord denies they will taste, having abandoned Zion like a watchtower in a vineyard and a little hut in a cucumber field, after they also rejected the last invitation in Christ. What from this order, according to the dispositions and preachings of the Creator, can be suitable to the one whose order does not have nor disposition to the conspiracy of the parable, who made the whole work once? Or what will be his first call, and what his second act of admonition? Others ought to excuse themselves first, then others ought to be called. Now, however, He comes to invite both parts equally, from the city, from the hedges, against the mirror of the parable. Nor can He judge the haughty ones whom He never invited before, whom He now approaches most of all. Or if He judges them for the future, despising the call, therefore He also portends the collection of their place from the nations for the future. Clearly, He will come again: [to preach to the nations. And if] He will come, I think, not as one calling the guests again, but already assigning. Meanwhile, you who interpret the call of this dinner into the heavenly banquet of spiritual saturation and joy, remember also that the earthly promises of wine and oil and grain and the city itself are equally figured into spiritual things by the Creator.

pass_b_english: What kind of people does He command to be invited to lunch or dinner? He showed us through Isaiah: break your bread for the hungry, and bring the poor and the homeless into your house — people who, obviously, cannot repay this kindness. If Christ forbids angling for that repayment here, promising it instead in the resurrection, that is the Creator's signature: He takes no pleasure in those who love gifts, but in those who pursue recompense. (Isaiah 58:7)

Now weigh the parable of the host: to whom does it more properly belong? A certain man prepared a great dinner and invited many. That dinner's preparation plainly figures the satisfaction of eternal life. First point: strangers and those with no claim are not the ones usually summoned to a feast; it is household members and family. Therefore the invitation belongs to the Creator, to whom the invitees belonged — through Adam as human beings, and through the patriarchs as Jews — not to a god to whom they belonged neither by nature nor by privilege.

Next, if the one who prepared the dinner sends a summons to the guests, the dinner is the Creator's as well: He sent word to those already called through the patriarchs, now to be admonished through the prophets. This is not a god who sent no one to warn them and did nothing beforehand to call them, only to descend suddenly — merely making Himself known as inviter, merely inviting as He already compels them into the banquet, collapsing the hour of dining and the hour of invitation into one.

The invited make excuses. If they were summoned by some other god, their refusal is justified, because the call came suddenly; if not justified, then the call was not sudden. But if not sudden, then it came from the Creator, from whom they received the call long ago — and whose call they then rejected, first saying to Aaron, 'Make us gods to go before us,' and from then on hearing with their ears but not hearing, the call of the God who fits this parable most precisely through Jeremiah: 'Listen to my voice, and I will be your God and you shall be my people; walk in all the ways I command you' — there is the invitation — 'but they did not listen, nor did they turn their ear' — there is the people's refusal — 'but they walked in the stubbornness of their evil hearts: I bought a field, I bought oxen, I took a wife.' (Jeremiah 7:23)

And still He presses: 'I sent all my servants the prophets to you, rising early and sending them' — here is the Holy Spirit, the guests' admonisher — 'but my people did not listen, did not incline their ears, and stiffened their necks.' This was reported to the householder, who was then moved — and well that He was moved, since Marcion denies his god can be moved; so this one is mine. He then orders a roundup from the streets and alleys of the city.

Let us test whether this fits the sense of Jeremiah again: 'Have I become a wilderness to the house of Israel, or a land left desolate?' — that is: 'Do I lack people to call, or places to call them from?' — because my people said, 'We will not come to you.' So He sent to call others from the same city. Then, with room still to spare, He commanded gathering from the roads and hedges — that is, us from the foreign nations — by that very jealousy with which Deuteronomy says: 'I will hide my face from them and see what becomes of them in the end' — meaning others will take their place — 'for they are a perverse generation, children in whom there is no faith. They provoked me with a no-god, angered me with their idols; so I will provoke them with a no-people, anger them with a foolish nation' — in us, that is, whose hope the Jews groan over, and from whose taste the Lord says they will be barred, once Zion is abandoned like a watchtower in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, after they also rejected the final invitation in Christ. (Deuteronomy 32:21)

What in this sequence — according to the Creator's own dispositions and proclamations — can possibly suit the rival god, who has neither order nor disposition to match the parable's plot, who made the whole work at once? What would be his first call, and what his second act of admonition? Others must excuse themselves first; only then are others summoned. But now he comes inviting both groups at once — from the city, from the hedges — flatly contradicting the parable's mirror. Nor can he judge as haughty those he never invited before, whom he now confronts most aggressively. Or if he judges them for a future contempt of the call, then he also signals a future roundup from the nations to take their place. Clearly he must come a second time: [to preach to the nations. And if] he comes, I suspect it will not be to call guests again, but to seat them.

Meanwhile, you who read this dinner's invitation as the heavenly banquet of spiritual satisfaction and joy, remember that the Creator equally figures the earthly promises of wine, oil, grain, and the city itself into spiritual realities.

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. Scripture citations (Isaiah 58:7, Jeremiah 7:23, Deuteronomy 32:21) were correctly identified and applied to the corresponding Latin text. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that preserves the agency and theological distinctions of the original (e.g., 'the invitation belongs to the Creator', 'He then orders a roundup').
